definition: Woodpecker is a training-free five steps method to correct hallucinations from MLLMs.
details: Woodpecker is a training-free five steps method to correct hallucinations from MLLMs.

explainer.lead: Woodpecker is a training-free, five-step method to correct hallucinations from multimodal large language models (MLLMs). It matters because it fixes hallucinated output without additional training.

tiers.eli5: Instead of teaching the model all over again, it checks what the model said in a few steps and patches up the parts that were made up.
tiers.practitioner: It is applied as a post-hoc correction pipeline over MLLM outputs in five steps, with no training required. A pitfall is expecting it to change the underlying model rather than correct its outputs.
tiers.paperLevel: A training-free five-step method to correct hallucinations from MLLMs. No formula or explicit limits are given.

explainer.example: An MLLM produces a description containing a hallucinated detail; Woodpecker runs its five training-free steps and corrects the output.
